ai.definition: AI Agents for Autonomous Systems are software entities designed to operate autonomously in complex, dynamic environments. These agents leverage machine learning and AI techniques to make decisions based on their interactions with the environment.
ai.howItWorks: These agents continuously gather data from sensors or other inputs, process this information using machine learning models, and then take actions that optimize a predefined objective function. They can learn from past experiences, adapt to new situations, and improve over time without explicit programming for every scenario.
ai.problemSolved: AI Agents address the challenge of creating systems capable of making complex decisions in real-time environments where human oversight is impractical or impossible.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves developing algorithms, training models on large datasets, integrating these into software frameworks, and testing the agents in controlled and then real-world scenarios.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes data collection, model training, integration with hardware, and iterative testing to refine performance. This is often done using cloud computing resources for scalability and flexibility.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the quality and volume of training data, computational resources required for training models, and ongoing maintenance costs for software updates and improvements.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook suggests continued growth as more industries recognize the benefits of autonomous systems in complex decision-making processes. However, challenges such as regulatory approval and public acceptance will influence market penetration.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks are still evolving for AI-driven autonomous systems, with varying requirements depending on the application domain (e.g., transportation, healthcare).
ai.risks: Risks include potential bias in decision-making processes, cybersecurity threats, and ethical concerns related to autonomy. Additionally, there is a risk of over-reliance on these systems without adequate human oversight.
ai.profitability: Profitability depends on the specific application and market segment. Early adopters in industries like manufacturing or logistics may see significant cost savings and efficiency gains, but broader adoption faces challenges related to regulatory compliance and public trust.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on enhancing explainability of AI decisions, improving robustness against adversarial attacks, and expanding the range of applications where autonomous agents can operate effectively.

glossary.def: Systems capable of performing tasks without continuous human control.
A subset of AI that involves training models on data to make decisions or predictions without explicit programming.
A mathematical function used in optimization problems to determine the best solution based on certain criteria.

subsystems.name: Perception and input
subsystems.role: gathers data from sensors, APIs or users so the agent knows the current situation.

subsystems.name: Memory and world model
subsystems.role: stores past experience and domain knowledge to inform future decisions.

subsystems.name: Reasoning and planning
subsystems.role: decides the next action by combining learned policy with deliberate planning.
parts: large language model or policy network

subsystems.name: Tool and action interface
subsystems.role: turns decisions into real actions in software or the physical world.

subsystems.name: Verification and safety
subsystems.role: checks that proposed actions are safe and likely to succeed before they are taken.

subsystems.name: Learning and feedback loop
subsystems.role: improves the agent from experience over time.

buildSteps.title: Define the task and environment
buildSteps.detail: Specify what the agent must achieve, what actions are allowed, and what counts as success.

buildSteps.title: Build a simulation and data pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Create a physics or software simulator to generate safe, cheap experience, and instrument the real environment to log data.

buildSteps.title: Train or select a base model
buildSteps.detail: Start from a pretrained language model or train a reinforcement-learning policy on simulated tasks.

buildSteps.title: Integrate memory and tool use
buildSteps.detail: Connect the model to a retrieval store and a set of callable tools, and design the loop that lets it act, observe and try again.

buildSteps.title: Add verification and safety layers
buildSteps.detail: Wrap the agent with rule-based checks and model-based rollouts so unsafe or nonsensical actions are blocked before execution.

buildSteps.title: Close the learning loop
buildSteps.detail: Feed real outcomes back as reward signals, retrain or fine-tune the policy, and guard against reward hacking or drift.

buildSteps.title: Deploy, monitor and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Run the agent in a controlled setting, log everything, and continuously retrain as the environment or task changes.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with tool use
prerequisites.why: they provide the flexible reasoning layer that can call APIs and write code.

pathway.milestone: task-specific agents that use tools in a loop (e.g. coding assistants, web-browsing bots)
pathway.unlocks: automation of well-defined digital workflows with human oversight.

pathway.milestone: agents with persistent memory and self-checking in sandboxed environments
pathway.unlocks: longer, multi-step tasks that need context and error recovery.

pathway.milestone: agents that learn from real-world experience in controlled domains such as warehouse robots or grid balancing
general autonomous agents with verifiable safety guarantees
pathway.unlocks: deployment in open-ended physical and social settings.
